chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hafs, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Maintaining ties of kinship improves character, makes the hand generous, purifies the soul, increases sustenance, and delays death.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of maintaining family ties in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the ethical practice of silat al-arham to both inner purification and outer worldly blessings. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding how kinship ties serve as a means of divine grace, simultaneously enhancing moral character (khuluq) and ensuring material sustenance (rizq) and longevity (ajal).

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ali Bin al Hakam, from Hafs, from Abu Hamza,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Goodly relationships with the relatives improves the manners, and allows the palm (to be generous), and betters the self, and increases in the sustenance, and delays in the death’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hafs from abu Hamza from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Maintaining good relations with relatives improves moral behavior, opens the ability for generosity, helps one’s soul agree easily to be generous, increases one’s means of sustenance and delays the coming of death.”
